explainers.title: 2026 San Francisco Voter Guide for Board of Supervisors, District 8

district: District 10 (Bayview-Hunters Point, Potrero Hill, Dogpatch, Central Waterfront, India Basin, Visitacion Valley, Sunnydale, Candlestick Point, McLaren Park)
scope_plain: Only voters in Supervisor District 10. Ranked choice: you can rank up to 10 candidates, first choice in the first column. If no one has a majority of first choices, the last-place candidate is dropped and those ballots move to their next choice, until someone has a majority. Nonpartisan, so no party labels.
office_explainer: One of 11 supervisors, San Francisco's city council. Passes city laws and the city budget.
why_it_matters: Open seat with 10 candidates, the most crowded race on San Francisco ballots. Supervisor Shamann Walton is termed out. With this many names, second and later rankings may decide who wins.

candidates.name: Pearci "PJ" Bastiany III
candidates.background: Master of Public Administration student at USF; small business owner, martial arts instructor, and founder and CEO of MAFH. Ballot designation: MPA Graduate Student.

own_words.text: Promotes his Martial Arts Community Protection Initiative, combining mentorship, education, public safety and workforce development.
committed to restoring confidence in San Francisco

candidates.name: Dionjay (DJ) Brookter
candidates.background: Community advocate who has spent 16 years connecting residents to jobs and workforce training; grew up in the Central Valley. Ballot designation: Community Organizer.

own_words.text: My commitment is to listen, serve, and work every day to build a stronger District 10.
Says families are struggling with the cost of living, seniors worry about staying, and small businesses are fighting to stay open.

candidates.name: Deandra Bryant
candidates.background: Lifelong Bayview Hunters Point resident; in-home care (IHSS) provider and housing and parent advocate; mother of a child with autism. Ballot designation: Housing Advocate.

own_words.text: expanding homeownership opportunities, improving housing stability, increasing support for children with disabilities
Wants stronger public safety and more investment and resources for District 10.

candidates.name: Theo Ellington
candidates.background: Executive director of the Bayview Opera House; former city commissioner, Golden State Warriors public affairs director and Salvation Army homeless-services leader; third-generation San Franciscan. Ballot designation: Public Policy Director.

own_words.text: our southeast neighborhoods receive the same focus, urgency, and investment as the rest of San Francisco
affordable housing without displacement, clean streets and parks, real community policing

candidates.name: J.R. Eppler
candidates.background: Small-business attorney; former president of the Potrero Boosters Neighborhood Association. Ballot designation: Small Business Attorney.

own_words.text: Public safety grounded in proven crime reduction tactics, like community policing and foot patrols.
A community-centered approach to housing that serves working families.

candidates.name: Ellsworth "Ell" M. Jennison, Jr.
candidates.background: Carpenter who has lived on a houseboat on India Basin since 1980. Ballot designation: Union Carpenter.

own_words.text: Keep existing open space open, test Pier 68 for toxicity, and turn undeveloped bayfront land near Innes Avenue into a park.

candidates.name: Mike Trouble Lin
candidates.background: Small business consultant. His statement is two lines. Ballot designation: Small Business Consultant.

own_words.text: Speak Now to bring Taylor Swift to San Francisco

candidates.name: Jamo Muhammad
candidates.background: CEO of the We Got Winners Big Brother Program (KQED). He filed no statement in the voter pamphlet. Ballot designation: Father.

own_words.text: Says residents' 'legitimate concerns' are often overlooked by developers or city interests, and he would represent community needs as development pressures grow.
Says his family has been affected by contamination at the Hunters Point Shipyard and the city must get serious about whether it can be fully cleaned up.

candidates.name: Jessica Pessecow
candidates.background: Says she regularly attends City Hall commission and Board meetings; built a website pulling together city services and resources. Ballot designation: Nurse / Legal Representative.

own_words.text: I turn participation into practical action for District 10.
Wants funding for neighborhood infrastructure around Jackson Playground and the MLK Jr. Pool, and for SF General Hospital.

candidates.name: Shawn M. Richard
candidates.background: Founder and leader of Brothers Against Guns; more than 31 years of work in the Bayview. No ballot designation (his pamphlet statement gives his occupation as CEO / Executive Director).

own_words.text: committed to addressing critical issues such as youth violence, education, and homelessness
